long_biography.plain_text:
In 1970, Espinosa's father established Representaciones e Investigaciones Médicas as a Mexican drug distributor. The enterprise moved into production and assembled a patent portfolio centered on fixed-dose combinations. Leopoldo later became its senior executive, sharing ownership with his sibling Fernando as the business built a broad commercial network and sustained rapid growth.

Teva bought the operating companies, products and intellectual property for $2.3 billion in 2016. The exit converted the family's closely held business into the capital underpinning the brothers' fortunes. Litigation followed when the buyer challenged pre-acquisition representations. A New York judge rejected the fraud, rescission, punitive-damages and most related claims. The surviving contract dispute ended through a mutual settlement, after which the court dismissed it.
